findings.title: Viewer draws the 38 RF-HOUSE I-joist rafters without their SeatCut (decision #109 birdsmouth): the lower flange runs 31.7 mm below the plate top at the heel

evidence.measured: model.json roofs[RF-HOUSE].members: 38 members shape i_joist, every one with `seat` (heel on the bearing's outer face, seat_run 63.5 mm, plate_top_z 6.15315). Underside at the heel line = 6.1214 m, i.e. 31.7 mm BELOW plate top, so the engine notches each rafter (member_solid: `if member.seat is not None` runs before any shape test, so the GLB/IFC get a notched sweep). In the viewer bucket() sends `m.shape === "i_joist"` to buildIJoists (members.ts:237) before the raked/seated branch, and buildIJoists has no seat handling; seatedProfileVertices is reached only from buildRakedMesh (members.ts:358). Result: 3 plies with a square heel; the bottom flange and web penetrate the wall's top plate by 31.7 mm along the whole heel line, on all 38 rafters. Perpendicular depth is right (vertical 0.3372 m x cos 26.57 deg = 0.3016 m = 11 7/8 in).
evidence.expected: The viewer draws the same notched silhouette the engine resolves (heel plumb cut, 2 1/2 in seat on the plate top), or at least no member volume under the plate top.
evidence.method: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-colincatlin-Documents-NoCloud-TypeHaus/fc951bd3-20bf-434f-9b45-0a1dac7cd982/scratchpad/geometry-review/U1/seat_probe.py (z0 at heel = z0_m + slope*heel_s vs seat.plate_top_z_m); read members.ts bucket() order.

findings.source: Decision #109 (TJ-4000 p.31 R5 / APA D710A 10h: I-joist birdsmouth, flange bearing). Engine twin geometry_members._seated_sweep.
findings.proposed_fix: In buildIJoists, when m.seat is set clip the three plies at heelS (bottom flange and web start at the plate top inside the seat run) or route a seated i_joist through the sweep path with an I-shaped ring. Viewer-only; add a bucket test.

findings.title: buildSolid thickens every solid under 10 mm to 10 mm: a 1.6 mm sill gasket becomes a 10 mm slab whose sides coincide with the sill plate

evidence.measured: structure.ts:75 draws every non-sweep, non-mesh solid with `Math.max(solid.z1_m, solid.z0_m + 0.01)` (only window_return is exempt). Served solids under 10 mm: 91 flashing at 9.525 mm, 10 sill_gasket at 1.588 mm, 8 trellis and 3 tub_batt at 6.35 mm, 8 vent slices at 5.104 mm. W-B-S4-SILL-GASKET: z -0.34131..-0.33973 (1.588 mm), outline area 0.4187 m2, identical to W-B-S4-SILL (sill_plate, z -0.33973..-0.30163, area 0.4187 m2). The viewer extrudes the gasket to -0.33131, so 8.4 mm of its side faces lie exactly on the plate's side faces (different materials, sill-seal vs SPF): a z-fighting band along every basement sill. The radon vent is six stacked slices per run (JOG1..JOG6, each z0 = previous z1); the top end slices (JOG6, OUT6) are drawn 4.9 mm above the pipe's true top (5.9817 -> 5.9866 m) while JOG1/OUT1 hide inside the next slice.
evidence.expected: Draw the served z0_m..z1_m. A thin solid that is hard to see is a render-priority question (polygonOffset, which is deliberate elsewhere), not a geometry one; the 10 mm floor makes the model disagree with the GLB and the engine solids.
evidence.method: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-colincatlin-Documents-NoCloud-TypeHaus/fc951bd3-20bf-434f-9b45-0a1dac7cd982/scratchpad/geometry-review/U1/thin_solids.py : python over model.json solids (not sweep/body_mesh/finish_panels, category != window_return) with z1-z0 < 0.01; shapely area of gasket vs sill outline.

findings.source: Viewer arithmetic, no product source. Sill seal thickness is the catalog's (1/16 in).
findings.proposed_fix: Drop the +0.01 floor (keep the z1 <= z0 guard), and give sill_gasket/flashing a polygonOffset tier in solidMaterials.ts if they flicker against the plate.

findings.title: Latent re-derivations that match the engine today only because catlin does not exercise them

evidence.measured: Each differs from its engine twin by rule, not by number on catlin. (a) walls.ts topIsRaked = top_z0/top_z1 set; geometry_walls.layer_solids also tops out when only head_caps exist; all 6 head-cap walls (W-A-N1/N2/N2B/S1/S2/S3) are raked, and the cap equals the rake at their axis ends (0.0 mm over 11 samples each). (b) clampPiecesToBand makes a banded piece flat at the band top; the engine takes max(min(rake, band_top), band_bottom) per vertex; 0 of 475 banded layers sit on a raked wall. (c) storeyFloorTopM = max(member z1) + subfloor thickness and ROOM_FINISH_THICKNESS_M 0.02 fallback, not floor.deck_z0_m + deck_plane lift or room_finished_floor_elevation: equal for 36/37 rooms (max |diff| 0.5 mm; RM-GARAGE is a coating, no plane drawn). On the sloped FS-SG-BALCONY the single max(member z1) top is up to 61 mm above the local deck (members z1 max 3.0328 vs deck_z0 2.9718 + lift at the low end) but no room sits on that storey. (d) model_json_opening_parts keeps only GPrism solids; all 735 opening part solids on catlin are GPrism, but a GMesh/GSweep part would vanish silently. (e) alarm discs are a 127 x 38 mm drawing constant, the Alarm record serves no product size.
evidence.expected: Either the viewer reads the served quantity (deck_z0_m/deck_plane, room finished elevation) or a test pins the twin.
evidence.method: inline python over model.json (walls head_caps, layers z0/z1, rooms, floors) and engine load (room_finished_floor_elevation); parts_probe.py for the GPrism count.

findings.proposed_fix: Serve `floor_top_z_m` per room (the engine already computes it for alarms) and draw that; assert GPrism-only in opening_parts_json.
